1. Executive Summary & Operational Variance
Fourth-quarter (Q4) operations experienced severe production headwinds resulting in an efficiency
decline from 82.5% in Q2 to 70.8% in Q4 (an absolute reduction of -11.7%, representing a relative drop
of -14.18%). Total factory volume decreased to 10,500 assemblies, while operating expenses escalated
to $4,150,000 due to expedited freight and overtime maintenance labor.

3. Root Cause 2 & 3: CNC Hydraulic Failures & AOI Inspection Shifts
Plant Beta (Facility 2) sustained 42 hours of unscheduled hydraulic fluid seal maintenance in November,
forcing an emergency shutdown of CNC Milling cells. Concurrently, the introduction of a new automated optical
inspection (AOI) sensor array required extensive recalibration, slowing line throughput by 14%.

4. Mathematical Verification of Quarterly Variance (Q2 vs Q4)
Cross-Quarter Variance Calculations:
  - Efficiency Drop: Delta = 70.8% - 82.5% = -11.7% (Absolute Decrease)
  - Relative Efficiency Change = (-11.7% / 82.5%) * 100% = -14.18%
  - Total Volume Reduction: 12,500 Units - 10,500 Units = -2,000 Units (-16.0%)
  - Cost Inflation: $4,150,000 - $3,750,000 = +$400,000 (+10.67% increase in operating expenses)
  - Unit Cost Spike: $4,150,000 / 10,500 = $395.24/unit (vs $300.00/unit in Q2, +31.75% increase).
